items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: I think Georgie Jessel was the other one. We handed down, man, when you think about it

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah. He was closer than a brother to me. I felt he was closer. We could understand each other. We had a whistle that we crossed to each other, know the whistle, you know. It was good. We would call each other Mike. He never called me Bubbles. I never called him Buck. I called him Mike. Oh, we were two, we were two -- I don't think there's any other two negroes in the world like Buck and Bubbles -- no other two, uh-uh,

impossible. Because, first of all, we were so gullible on helpin', helpin' people and doing and loved to do benefits -- hospitals and urban league and all those things -- we loved to do that and we did that along with Bill Robinson. He likes to do benefits, too, he was King Benefit Man. King Benefit of the theatrical profession, he was, Bill Robinson. And I think somebody else -- I think Georgie Jessel was the other one. We handed down, man, when you think about it -- m-m-m. I'm going to do something, I don't…

I want to change the National Anthem. I want to change that song and I want to change NAACP. I want to change that. I want to change the AARP, they ain't doin' nothin' -- all people aged 65 and over should get all their information concerning their condition in any form or fashion from the AARP, that's where it should come, not from Social Security.
